static_findings.snippet: - Working in a directory containing `.move` files or `Move.toml`
- Find all `.move` files using glob patterns
- ✅ GOOD when importing members: `use my_package::my_module::{Self, Member};`
- ❌ BAD: `const NOT_AUTHORIZED: u64 = 0;` (all-caps reserved for regular constants)
- ❌ BAD: `const MyConstant: vector<u8> = b"value";` (PascalCase suggests error)
- ✅ GOOD: `public struct AdminCap has key, store { id: UID }`
- ❌ BAD: `public struct Admin has key, store { id: UID }` (unclear it's a capability)
- ❌ BAD: `public struct PromisePotato {}` (redundant, abilities show it's hot potato)
- ✅ GOOD: `public struct UserRegistered has copy, drop { user: address }`
- ❌ BAD: `public struct RegisterUser has copy, drop { user: address }` (ambiguous)
- ✅ CANONICAL: `public struct DynamicFieldKey() has copy, drop, store;`
- ⚠️ ACCEPTABLE: `public struct DynamicField has copy, drop, store {}`
- ✅ GOOD: `public fun do_something(): T { ... }` (composable, returns value)
- ❌ BAD: `public fun mint_and_transfer(ctx: &mut TxContext) { transfer::transfer(...) }` (not compos
- ❌ BAD: `public fun authorize(cap: &AdminCap, app: &mut App)` (breaks method associativity)
- ✅ GOOD: `public fun details_mut(u: &mut User): &mut Details` (mutable accessor)
- ❌ BAD: `use std::string::utf8; let str = utf8(b"hello, world!");`
- ❌ BAD: `let mut my_vec = vector::empty(); vector::push_back(&mut my_vec, 10);`
- ✅ GOOD: `let sum = source.fold!(0, |acc, v| acc + v);`
- ✅ GOOD: `let filtered = source.filter!(|e| e > 10);` (requires T: drop)
- ❌ BAD: `let MyStruct { id, field_1: _, field_2: _, field_3: _ } = value;`
- ❌ BAD: Separate `#[test]` and `#[expected_failure]` on different lines
- ✅ GOOD: End with `abort` to show failure point
- ❌ BAD: Include `test.end()` or other cleanup in expected_failure tests
- ❌ BAD: `#[test] fun test_this_feature() { }` (redundant in test module)
- ✅ GOOD for simple tests: `let ctx = &mut tx_context::dummy();`
- ❌ BAD: `assert!(is_success, 0);` (may conflict with app error codes)
- ✅ GOOD: `assert_eq!(result, expected_value);` (shows both values on failure)
- **Testing** - Use simplest approach that works; avoid over-engineering

content.value_statement: Move projects need consistent review against modern Move 2024 and Sui guidance. This skill checks packages, manifests, tests, and style against the Move Book checklist.
actual_capabilities: Detects Move projects by looking for Move.toml and .move files.
Checks package manifests for Move 2024 edition, implicit Sui dependencies, and named address conventions.
Reviews modules, imports, constants, structs, functions, and parameter ordering against checklist rules.
Evaluates Move 2024 macro usage, option handling, vector patterns, and method chaining style.
Reviews tests for expected failure attributes, assertion style, cleanup patterns, and naming.
Formats findings with file references, impact, recommended changes, and next steps.
limitations: It relies on repository contents supplied by the user and does not compile Move code by itself.
It focuses on code quality conventions, not full smart contract security verification.
It may need user guidance for large packages or category-specific reviews.
Its recommendations follow the included Move Book checklist and may lag newer ecosystem changes.

use_cases.title: Pre-review cleanup
use_cases.description: Find Move 2024 style issues before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Package standards audit
use_cases.description: Check manifests, modules, and naming patterns across a Sui package.

use_cases.title: Test quality review
use_cases.description: Review Move tests for expected failures, assertions, cleanup, and simple setup.

prompt_templates.title: Review a package
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Move package against the Move Book code quality checklist. Start with Move.toml, then review source files. Report critical issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Check manifest quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Move.toml for Move 2024 edition, framework dependencies, and named address conventions. Explain each issue and recommended change.

prompt_templates.title: Review tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Move test modules in this package. Focus on expected failure attributes, assertion style, cleanup patterns, and unnecessary test scenario usage.

prompt_templates.title: Audit release readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release readiness code quality audit for this Sui Move package. Prioritize manifest, syntax, function design, macros, tests, and documentation issues.

output_examples.input: Review a Sui Move package before pull request merge.
output_examples.output: A prioritized report listing Move 2024 manifest issues, outdated syntax, test cleanup concerns, and recommended next steps.

output_examples.input: Check whether a function signature follows project standards.
output_examples.output: A concise review of parameter order, visibility choice, composability, and naming, with a recommended shape described in prose.

output_examples.input: Audit Move tests for checklist compliance.
output_examples.output: A test-focused summary covering expected failures, assertion style, simple context setup, and cleanup risks.

best_practices: Run it from the package root so the skill can inspect Move.toml and source files.
Ask for a focused category review when you only need manifest, tests, or function style.
Review critical Move 2024 edition findings before applying lower priority style changes.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a substitute for formal smart contract security review.
Requesting automatic fixes before reading the prioritized findings.
Running broad reviews without specifying package scope in large monorepos.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Move packages, manifests, tests, and style against the Move Book Code Quality Checklist.

faq.question: Does it support Sui Move projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes Sui Move patterns, Sui 1.45 dependency handling, and Move 2024 Edition conventions.

faq.question: Can it fix issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest fixes and may help apply them when the user asks, but findings should be reviewed first.

faq.question: Is this a security audit tool?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on code quality and maintainability, not complete smart contract security assurance.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide access to Move.toml and relevant .move files, plus the review scope they want.
